notice: Main plot compares VCO total PM-SSB simulation and gm pair flicker + modeled thermal. flicker harmonics combine coherently; thermal independent input bands and independent noise sources add in power. unmodeled sources remain in the simulated total.

calculated_vs_total_db.label: Calculated minus simulated total
calculated_vs_total_db.meaning: Calculated phase noise for the selected noise filter minus total VCO PM-SSB simulated phase noise.
calculated_vs_total_db.purpose: Compare modeled coverage with all-source noise. Flicker-only or thermal-only results are not expected to equal the all-source reference.
calculated_vs_total_db.scope: currently filtered symmetric pair / passive-network calculation, compared against whole VCO

thermal_noise.label: Thermal and calculated total
thermal_noise.meaning: Thermal noise is calculated from periodic MOS source PSD and static passive-LC source PSD through pure PM transfer. The two symmetric gm devices add independently in power.
thermal_noise.purpose: Compare individual device/mechanism contributions against HBNoise. Missing data remain N/A; flicker does not substitute for thermal noise.
thermal_noise.scope: symmetric gm pair + supported passive loss sources, excludes other active devices/shot noise

point.label: Result sample
point.meaning: Result record for one actual design operating point and offset.
point.purpose: Locate raw simulation and exported results without mixing offsets.

operating_point_id.label: Design operating point
operating_point_id.meaning: Operating-point identity determined by corner, device and bias parameters; evaluation offset is excluded.
operating_point_id.purpose: Connect offset samples only within the same operating point.

operating_parameters.label: Actual operating parameters
operating_parameters.meaning: Effective design-parameter snapshot saved with the result, including values such as SW, temperature or supply settings. Evaluation offset is excluded.
operating_parameters.purpose: Check that corner and design variables took effect and remain traceable after migration. Later form edits are not used.
operating_parameters.formula: effective parameter snapshot of the selected run

corner.label: Corner name
corner.meaning: Maestro corner label. The same label may contain multiple design points.
corner.purpose: Check result ownership; a shared name alone does not justify merging data.

offset_Hz.label: Offset
offset_Hz.meaning: Frequency distance between the noise evaluation point and oscillator carrier.
offset_Hz.purpose: Select the harmonic table and phase-noise x coordinate. This is not a design-point index.

f0_Hz.label: Oscillation frequency
f0_Hz.meaning: Oscillation frequency actually obtained at the selected operating point.
f0_Hz.purpose: Set harmonic frequencies and the periodic phase axis, and check that operating-point changes took effect.

period_s.label: Oscillation period
period_s.meaning: Duration of one complete oscillation period.
period_s.purpose: Interpret periodic waveforms and time-domain sample positions.

carrier_peak_V.label: Differential carrier peak
carrier_peak_V.meaning: Peak fundamental amplitude of the selected positive-minus-negative output; this is not RMS amplitude.
carrier_peak_V.purpose: Normalize output noise to dBc/Hz. Mixing peak and RMS conventions introduces a 3 dB error.
carrier_peak_V.scope: current output direction and operating point

mDC_cycle_mean_A_rtHz.label: Quasi-static noise period mean
mDC_cycle_mean_A_rtHz.meaning: Mean noise-amplitude waveform obtained by DC-noise sampling along the periodic VCO bias trajectory.
mDC_cycle_mean_A_rtHz.purpose: Establish the quasi-static noise baseline. This quantity is not output phase noise.

mDyn_rms_A_rtHz.label: Dynamic noise modulation RMS
mDyn_rms_A_rtHz.meaning: RMS of the dynamically corrected noise-modulation waveform over one period.
mDyn_rms_A_rtHz.purpose: Summarize modulation strength; this is not the output noise after ISF summation.

dynamic_pm_asd_V_rtHz.label: Dynamically calculated noise ASD
dynamic_pm_asd_V_rtHz.meaning: Output noise ASD from the coherent sum of complex harmonic contributions. A PM interpretation requires the recorded PM approximation checks.
dynamic_pm_asd_V_rtHz.purpose: Compare with the Spectre reference for the same device and mechanism.

spectre_fn_pm_asd_V_rtHz.label: Spectre Single-device reference ASD
spectre_fn_pm_asd_V_rtHz.meaning: Intrinsic flicker PM-SSB output contribution of the target device, extracted from Spectre HBNOISE.
spectre_fn_pm_asd_V_rtHz.purpose: Provide a simulation reference for single-device closure.
spectre_fn_pm_asd_V_rtHz.scope: target single device flicker, not whole VCO

predicted_pair_pm_asd_V_rtHz.label: Two-device calculation ASD
predicted_pair_pm_asd_V_rtHz.meaning: Output noise of two independent devices combined in power. The symmetric replica assumption is identified separately.
predicted_pair_pm_asd_V_rtHz.purpose: Check two-device contributions against the two-device reference, rather than a single-device or whole-circuit reference.

spectre_pair_pm_asd_V_rtHz.label: Spectre two-device reference ASD
spectre_pair_pm_asd_V_rtHz.meaning: Power sum of the flicker PM contributions of two independent devices extracted from Spectre.
spectre_pair_pm_asd_V_rtHz.purpose: Compare with the two-device calculation using the same scope.
spectre_pair_pm_asd_V_rtHz.scope: independent device pair flicker, not whole VCO

dynamic_dBc_Hz.label: ISF calculated phase noise
dynamic_dBc_Hz.meaning: Single-device equivalent phase noise from the dynamic coherent sum, normalized by the differential peak carrier. The PM approximation must also be valid.
dynamic_dBc_Hz.purpose: Provide the calculated value for the main comparison curve.

spectre_fn_dBc_Hz.label: Target single-device simulation flicker Phase noise
spectre_fn_dBc_Hz.meaning: Intrinsic flicker PM-SSB contribution of the target device in VCO HBNOISE, rather than the whole-VCO total.
spectre_fn_dBc_Hz.purpose: Compare with single-device ISF at the same scope in the single-offset contribution table.

spectre_total_dBc_Hz.label: VCO simulated total phase noise
spectre_total_dBc_Hz.meaning: Total HBNOISE PM-SSB at the output of this private VCO simulation, using the same carrier normalization. It includes flicker, thermal and all other simulated noise sources.
spectre_total_dBc_Hz.purpose: Provide the actual simulation curve. Its scope exceeds device-only flicker ISF, so a difference does not by itself prove an algorithm error. Legacy missing data are not replaced by a single-device value.

spectre_total_pm_asd_V_rtHz.label: VCO total PM-SSB Noise ASD
spectre_total_pm_asd_V_rtHz.meaning: Raw total PM-SSB noise ASD at the VCO HBNOISE output.
spectre_total_pm_asd_V_rtHz.purpose: Trace total phase-noise conversion and source fractions.

spectre_noise_contributions.label: Simulated noise source details
spectre_noise_contributions.meaning: Raw device and noise-mechanism contributions for the same VCO, operating point and offset.
spectre_noise_contributions.purpose: Distinguish flicker, thermal and other sources. Aggregate comparison rows overlap source details and must not be counted twice.

spectre_noise_reference.label: Total-noise extraction source
spectre_noise_reference.meaning: Actual VCO simulation data, analysis and sideband convention used for extraction.
spectre_noise_reference.purpose: Distinguish the private simulation from historical Maestro scalars and support independent review.

predicted_pair_dBc_Hz.label: Two-device calculated phase noise
predicted_pair_dBc_Hz.meaning: Phase noise obtained by normalizing the independent two-device power sum with the same carrier.
predicted_pair_dBc_Hz.purpose: Compare only with the two-device simulation curve and check the symmetry assumption.

spectre_pair_dBc_Hz.label: Two-device simulated phase noise
spectre_pair_dBc_Hz.meaning: Phase noise associated with the two devices' Spectre flicker contributions.
spectre_pair_dBc_Hz.purpose: Provide the two-device closure reference; this is not total VCO phase noise.

dc_dBc_Hz.label: Quasi-static phase-noise calculation
dc_dBc_Hz.meaning: ISF sum using quasi-static noise Fourier coefficients.
dc_dBc_Hz.purpose: Compare with the dynamic method to assess the importance of dynamic correction.

delay_dBc_Hz.label: Uniform-delay phase-noise approximation
delay_dBc_Hz.meaning: Phase-noise estimate with only a uniform time delay added to the quasi-static coefficients.
delay_dBc_Hz.purpose: Test whether one global delay describes the dynamic phase of each harmonic.

dc_pm_asd_V_rtHz.label: Quasi-static output ASD
dc_pm_asd_V_rtHz.meaning: Coherent output magnitude from quasi-static noise coefficients and signed transfer functions.
dc_pm_asd_V_rtHz.purpose: Provide a closure baseline for the static method.

delay_pm_asd_V_rtHz.label: Uniform-delay output ASD
delay_pm_asd_V_rtHz.meaning: Output magnitude from quasi-static noise coefficients with a uniform delay.
delay_pm_asd_V_rtHz.purpose: Compare the simple delay model with full dynamic correction.

dynamic_error_dB.label: Single-device dynamic error
dynamic_error_dB.meaning: Dynamic calculation error relative to the same-device Spectre reference. Positive values overestimate; negative values underestimate.
dynamic_error_dB.purpose: Assess absolute closure. This alone does not establish signoff.

pair_error_dB.label: Two-device error
pair_error_dB.meaning: Independent two-device power-sum calculation error relative to the two-device Spectre reference.
pair_error_dB.purpose: Check two-device closure and the symmetry assumption.

dc_error_dB.label: Quasi-static method error
dc_error_dB.meaning: Quasi-static method error relative to the single-device Spectre reference.
dc_error_dB.purpose: Identify the deviation introduced by the static approximation.

delay_error_dB.label: Uniform-delay method error
delay_error_dB.meaning: Uniform-delay approximation error relative to the single-device reference.
delay_error_dB.purpose: Assess whether a simple time shift is sufficient.

k.label: Harmonic order
k.meaning: Order of periodic noise modulation. For k>0, Qk includes both positive and negative sidebands.
k.purpose: Distinguish harmonic contributions; do not confuse k with Maestro design-point indices.
k.formula: Harmonic frequency k·f0; HBXF sideband = k−1

Mdc_mag_A_rtHz.label: |Mdc,k| quasi-static coefficient
Mdc_mag_A_rtHz.meaning: Magnitude of the order-k Fourier coefficient of the quasi-static noise-amplitude modulation waveform.
Mdc_mag_A_rtHz.purpose: Provide the baseline for dynamic magnitude and phase correction.
Mdc_mag_A_rtHz.scope: target single device flicker, order k

Mdyn_mag_A_rtHz.label: |Mdyn,k| dynamic coefficient
Mdyn_mag_A_rtHz.meaning: Magnitude of the order-k noise-modulation coefficient from the dynamic replica and engineering phase candidate.
Mdyn_mag_A_rtHz.purpose: Provide the noise input for coherent summation.
Mdyn_mag_A_rtHz.scope: target single device flicker, order k

Mdc_phase_deg.label: Mdc Phase
Mdc_phase_deg.meaning: Phase of the quasi-static coefficient relative to the shared VCO period time origin.
Mdc_phase_deg.purpose: Compare with dynamic phase. Do not shift waveforms to fit results.

Mdyn_phase_deg.label: Mdyn Phase
Mdyn_phase_deg.meaning: Dynamic coefficient phase of the selected engineering candidate, not a direct measurement of instantaneous random-noise phase.
Mdyn_phase_deg.purpose: Determine harmonic reinforcement or cancellation, together with HBAC secondary validation evidence.

A_k.label: Ak Magnitude correction
A_k.meaning: Magnitude ratio of dynamic to quasi-static coefficients.
A_k.purpose: Values near 1 indicate a small magnitude correction. The ratio is physically undefined for a zero denominator.

delta_k_deg.label: δk Phase correction
delta_k_deg.meaning: Dynamic phase change relative to quasi-static phase.
delta_k_deg.purpose: Assess how dynamic effects change harmonic reinforcement and cancellation.

Ck_real.label: Ck real part
Ck_real.meaning: Real part of the complex dynamic correction coefficient.
Ck_real.purpose: Describe dynamic correction jointly through magnitude Ak and phase δk.

Ck_imag.label: Ck imaginary part
Ck_imag.meaning: Imaginary part of the complex dynamic correction coefficient.
Ck_imag.purpose: Preserve phase information together with the real part of Ck.

Q_real_V_rtHz.label: Qk real part
Q_real_V_rtHz.meaning: Real part of the order-k complex output contribution, combining positive and negative sidebands.
Q_real_V_rtHz.purpose: Sum coherently with the imaginary part; this is not independent noise power.
Q_real_V_rtHz.scope: target single device flicker, order k

Q_imag_V_rtHz.label: Qk imaginary part
Q_imag_V_rtHz.meaning: Imaginary part of the order-k complex output contribution.
Q_imag_V_rtHz.purpose: Preserve relative harmonic phases and cancellation.
Q_imag_V_rtHz.scope: target single device flicker, order k

Q_mag_V_rtHz.label: |Qk| Single-order magnitude
Q_mag_V_rtHz.meaning: Magnitude of one harmonic group's complex output contribution.
Q_mag_V_rtHz.purpose: Inspect strength by order. Squared magnitudes cannot simply be added to obtain the total.

Q_phase_deg.label: ∠Qk Contribution phase
Q_phase_deg.meaning: Angle of a single-order complex output contribution.
Q_phase_deg.purpose: Explain reinforcement or cancellation when combined with other harmonics.

cum_real_V_rtHz.label: ΣQ real part
cum_real_V_rtHz.meaning: Real part of the cumulative complex sum from k=0 through the current order.
cum_real_V_rtHz.purpose: Construct cumulative phase noise and complex-plane closure plots.

cum_imag_V_rtHz.label: ΣQ imaginary part
cum_imag_V_rtHz.meaning: Imaginary part of the cumulative complex sum from k=0 through the current order.
cum_imag_V_rtHz.purpose: Determine cumulative noise jointly with the real part, retaining phase.

cum_mag_V_rtHz.label: |ΣQ| Cumulative magnitude
cum_mag_V_rtHz.meaning: Magnitude of the coherent complex sum. It can decrease as more harmonics are included.
cum_mag_V_rtHz.purpose: Inspect how harmonic truncation affects output results.
cum_mag_V_rtHz.scope: from order zero through the current order

harmonic_equivalent_dBc_Hz.label: Single-order equivalent phase noise
harmonic_equivalent_dBc_Hz.meaning: Carrier-normalized equivalent contribution from this harmonic group alone; it is not independent additive noise power.
harmonic_equivalent_dBc_Hz.purpose: Inspect individual orders versus offset alongside the coherent sum.
harmonic_equivalent_dBc_Hz.scope: target single device flicker, order k

cumulative_dBc_Hz.label: Cumulative phase noise
cumulative_dBc_Hz.meaning: Carrier-normalized coherent sum from order zero through the current order.
cumulative_dBc_Hz.purpose: Assess harmonic truncation and cancellation; this is not total VCO phase noise.

cumulative_error_dB.label: Cumulative closure error
cumulative_error_dB.meaning: Error of the current harmonic-truncation result relative to the single-device Spectre reference.
cumulative_error_dB.purpose: Check whether adding harmonics improves closure. Positive values overestimate; negative values underestimate.

pair_harmonic_equivalent_dBc_Hz.label: Two-device single-order equivalent phase noise
pair_harmonic_equivalent_dBc_Hz.meaning: Order-k Qk on the representative side, with power doubled for a symmetric independent gm pair. Harmonics remain mutually coherent.
pair_harmonic_equivalent_dBc_Hz.purpose: Inspect each order versus offset. Do not add the per-order dB values.
pair_harmonic_equivalent_dBc_Hz.scope: symmetric gm pair flicker, order k

pair_cumulative_dBc_Hz.label: Two-device coherent cumulative phase noise
pair_cumulative_dBc_Hz.meaning: Signed complex sum on the representative side from zero through the current order, followed by power addition of the two independent symmetric devices.
pair_cumulative_dBc_Hz.purpose: Assess harmonic truncation and cancellation; this is not total VCO phase noise.

sqrt_Sxi_A_rtHz.label: Shared underlying noise ASD
sqrt_Sxi_A_rtHz.meaning: Underlying flicker normalization amplitude shared by all harmonics, with the square root taken once.
sqrt_Sxi_A_rtHz.purpose: Prevent an independent source per harmonic or repeated square roots.

Dk_real.label: Dk real part
Dk_real.meaning: Real part of the dynamic modulation coefficient divided by the shared source ASD.
Dk_real.purpose: Check that all harmonics share the same underlying source.

Dk_imag.label: Dk imaginary part
Dk_imag.meaning: Imaginary part of the shared-source-normalized dynamic modulation coefficient.
Dk_imag.purpose: Preserve modulation phase jointly with the real part.

AM_A_rtHz.label: AM Current noise ASD
AM_A_rtHz.meaning: AM noise magnitude near this harmonic in the dynamic noise replica.
AM_A_rtHz.purpose: Constrain engineering phase candidates jointly with PM and both sidebands.

PM_A_rtHz.label: PM Current noise ASD
PM_A_rtHz.meaning: PM noise magnitude near this harmonic in the dynamic noise replica.
PM_A_rtHz.purpose: Constrain phase candidates jointly with AM. Magnitude alone cannot uniquely determine random-noise phase.

USB_A_rtHz.label: Upper-sideband noise ASD
USB_A_rtHz.meaning: Noise ASD of this harmonic's upper sideband.

LSB_A_rtHz.label: Lower-sideband noise ASD
LSB_A_rtHz.meaning: Noise ASD of this harmonic's lower sideband.
LSB_A_rtHz.purpose: Preserve sideband asymmetry and avoid reading only one sideband.

HBAC_norm_mag.label: HBAC Normalized magnitude
HBAC_norm_mag.meaning: Magnitude of deterministic small-signal injection response relative to its order-zero response.
HBAC_norm_mag.purpose: Provide a secondary diagnostic for engineering phase candidates, without directly replacing noise ASD.

HBAC_norm_phase_deg.label: HBAC Normalized phase
HBAC_norm_phase_deg.meaning: Phase of deterministic injection relative to its order-zero response.
HBAC_norm_phase_deg.purpose: Support a secondary modulation-phase check. It is not random-noise phase.

HBAC_vs_Mdyn_phase_deg.label: HBAC phase difference from candidate
HBAC_vs_Mdyn_phase_deg.meaning: Wrapped phase difference between deterministic injection response and the dynamic-noise engineering candidate.
HBAC_vs_Mdyn_phase_deg.purpose: Identify potentially unreliable phase-model orders, considering magnitude and validation conditions together.

Id_mag_A.label: Drain-current harmonic magnitude
Id_mag_A.meaning: Magnitude of the order-k Fourier coefficient of periodic drain current.
Id_mag_A.purpose: Provide a reference for periodic conduction and noise-modulation phase.

Id_phase_deg.label: Drain-current harmonic phase
Id_phase_deg.meaning: Phase of the periodic drain-current coefficient relative to the shared period origin.
Id_phase_deg.purpose: Provide the current reference for engineering phase selection.

uniform_delay_s.label: Uniform-delay fit
uniform_delay_s.meaning: Time delay fitted from the slope of the per-order static/dynamic phase difference.
uniform_delay_s.purpose: Diagnose the uniform-delay approximation without changing raw waveform time origins.

candidate_score.label: Engineering phase candidate score
candidate_score.meaning: Candidate cost based on static phase, delay smoothness and continuity; lower is better.
candidate_score.purpose: Explain candidate selection. This is not statistical confidence and is not fitted from final phase-noise error.
candidate_score.formula: defined weighted sum of candidate costs

chosen_signs.label: Selected phase candidate
chosen_signs.meaning: Engineering branch chosen from nonnegative AM and ±PM, referenced to current harmonics. The candidate set may omit the true phase.
chosen_signs.purpose: Make the phase assumption reviewable and reproducible. Selecting a branch does not prove the quadrant.
chosen_signs.formula: per-order branch AM ± jPM combination, then rotate to the current reference

pm_magnitude_projection_valid.label: PM Magnitude approximation check
pm_magnitude_projection_valid.meaning: Whether AM is sufficiently small relative to PM to label complex output magnitude approximately as PM noise.
pm_magnitude_projection_valid.purpose: Assess the physical interpretation of equivalent phase noise. Unknown does not mean pass.
pm_magnitude_projection_valid.formula: AM/PM ratio does not exceed the defined threshold

spectre_am_to_pm_dB.label: AM/PM magnitude ratio
spectre_am_to_pm_dB.meaning: Ratio of Spectre AM noise to PM noise for the target device.
spectre_am_to_pm_dB.purpose: Check whether AM is small enough for the current PM magnitude approximation.

numerical_quality_pass.label: Simulation numerical quality
numerical_quality_pass.meaning: Whether the logs pass the existing numerical-quality warning checks in addition to zero-error completion.
numerical_quality_pass.purpose: Avoid treating simulations with significant numerical warnings as reliable signoff.

hbac_secondary_validation_pass.label: HBAC Phase-difference threshold check
hbac_secondary_validation_pass.meaning: Whether per-order phase differences between deterministic injection and engineering candidates meet the threshold. This does not prove injection equivalence or the correct quadrant.
hbac_secondary_validation_pass.purpose: Secondary diagnostic only. An analytic reference has a 40° phase error that still passes the 45° threshold, so this is not golden-reference validation.

hbac_max_phase_delta_deg.label: Maximum HBAC phase difference
hbac_max_phase_delta_deg.meaning: Largest HBAC-to-candidate phase difference among nonzero harmonics at this sample.
hbac_max_phase_delta_deg.purpose: Identify whether per-order phase validation requires inspection.

hbac_phase_warn_threshold_deg.label: HBAC Phase threshold
hbac_phase_warn_threshold_deg.meaning: Secondary phase-difference threshold used for this run; it is not a criterion for true random-noise phase.
hbac_phase_warn_threshold_deg.purpose: Explain threshold status. A wrong quadrant can fall below the threshold; later form values must not overwrite historical settings.

heff_carrier_i_signed.label: Effective ISF-I projection
heff_carrier_i_signed.meaning: Signed integral of the carrier-referenced I ISF branch with noise modulation.
heff_carrier_i_signed.purpose: Validate the real branch of complex physical output while retaining signs.

heff_carrier_q_signed.label: Effective ISF-Q projection
heff_carrier_q_signed.meaning: Signed integral of the carrier-referenced Q ISF branch with noise modulation.
heff_carrier_q_signed.purpose: Validate the imaginary branch of complex physical output without omitting it.

heff_branch_rss.label: ISF Two-branch synthesis
heff_branch_rss.meaning: Root-sum-square combination of I/Q branches at a fixed carrier reference.
heff_branch_rss.purpose: Independently check algebraic consistency against coherent summation in physical units.

gamma_exact_equivalence_error_dB.label: ISF Algebraic equivalence error
gamma_exact_equivalence_error_dB.meaning: Relative difference between two-branch ISF synthesis and the physical-unit output calculation.
gamma_exact_equivalence_error_dB.purpose: Check units and both sidebands. This does not validate the physical noise model itself.

pair_model.label: Two-device model assumption
pair_model.meaning: Whether the second device is approximated by an independent symmetric model.
pair_model.purpose: Avoid presenting doubled single-device power as independent calculations of two different devices.
